## Structure and components

- [statement] Spillantini and colleagues report that Lewy bodies and Lewy neurites contain abnormal filamentous alpha-synuclein material. (low confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/18591134/ · keywords: Alpha-synucleinopathies: PD, DLB and MSA
- [statement] Schweighauser and colleagues report two filament types in the MSA brains studied, each composed of two different protofilaments. (low confidence) — https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-020-2317-6 · keywords: Alpha-synucleinopathies: PD, DLB and MSA

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] Spillantini and colleagues classify Parkinson's disease, dementia with Lewy bodies and multiple system atrophy as alpha-synucleinopathies; Shahnawaz and colleagues likewise group them as diseases associated with α-synuclein misfolding and aggregation. (high confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/18591134/ · keywords: Alpha-synucleinopathies: PD, DLB and MSA · also: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-020-1984-7
- [statement] Shahnawaz and colleagues note that clinical differentiation of Parkinson’s disease and multiple system atrophy is challenging, particularly early in disease. (low confidence) — https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-020-1984-7 · keywords: Alpha-synucleinopathies: PD, DLB and MSA
- [statement] Shahnawaz and colleagues report that their α-synuclein-PMCA assay discriminated cerebrospinal fluid samples from patients diagnosed with Parkinson’s disease from those with multiple system atrophy. (low confidence) — https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-020-1984-7 · keywords: Alpha-synucleinopathies: PD, DLB and MSA

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] Schweighauser and colleagues report that MSA brain-extracted α-synuclein filament structures differ from structures formed in vitro using recombinant proteins. (low confidence) — https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-020-2317-6 · keywords: Alpha-synucleinopathies: PD, DLB and MSA

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Yang and colleagues describe MSA α-synuclein inclusions as especially prominent in oligodendrocytes, consistent with the glial cytoplasmic inclusions described by Spillantini and colleagues. (medium confidence) — https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-022-05319-3 · keywords: Alpha-synucleinopathies: PD, DLB and MSA · also: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/18591134/
- [statement] Lee and colleagues describe neuronal soma Lewy bodies and axonal or dendritic Lewy neurites in PD, PDD and DLB. (low confidence) — https://elifesciences.org/articles/92775 · keywords: Alpha-synucleinopathies: PD, DLB and MSA
- [statement] Yang and colleagues report a single-protofilament Lewy fold in α-synuclein filaments extracted from the brains of individuals with PD, PDD and DLB. (low confidence) — https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-022-05319-3 · keywords: Alpha-synucleinopathies: PD, DLB and MSA
- [statement] Schweighauser and colleagues report non-proteinaceous molecules at the protofilament interface in each MSA filament type studied. (low confidence) — https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-020-2317-6 · keywords: Alpha-synucleinopathies: PD, DLB and MSA
- [statement] Lee and colleagues specify that their study used RT-QuIC and referred to that method as SAA. (low confidence) — https://elifesciences.org/articles/92775 · keywords: Alpha-synucleinopathies: PD, DLB and MSA
- [statement] Lee and colleagues report that their SAA fibrils failed to adopt the biochemical, structural and post-translational modification properties of the brain-derived seed fibrils. (low confidence) — https://elifesciences.org/articles/92775 · keywords: Alpha-synucleinopathies: PD, DLB and MSA
- [statement] The author correction to the MSA filament paper states that a duplicated DLB comparison image was replaced with the correct image. (low confidence) (verified as of 2025-10-22) — https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-025-09700-w · keywords: Alpha-synucleinopathies: PD, DLB and MSA
